title: Unify icon-button densities and chart/table spacing; add publish gating with visual diffing
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: multiple icon button variants (dense, compact, default) have inconsistent internal padding, icon sizing, and token usage across the Figma library. Similarly, chart and table atoms use a mix of hard-coded spacers and token aliases, leading to visual drift and flaky snapshots during releases. Goal: consolidate button sizes into a single size-token contract, normalize chart/table internal padding to semantic spacing tokens, and add a publish gating pipeline that runs visual diffs for library changes before release. Outcomes: fewer ad-hoc overrides, consistent accessibility hit areas, predictable published library updates, and automated regression detection via screenshot diffs.
acceptance_criteria: A single set of button size tokens (btn-xs, btn-sm, btn-md) exists in Figma and maps to design tokens in the token source file
All icon buttons use the new tokenized padding and 24px/20px icon scaling rules; no component has hard-coded pixel padding
Chart and table primitives replace hard-coded spacers with token aliases and expose a small set of padding props (cellPadding, rowGap, chartInner)
Publish gating: Figma library publish triggers a CI job that captures screenshots of affected frames and runs a visual diff; failures block publish and create a GitHub PR template with diffs
Documentation: Confluence guide updated with migration steps, accessibility rationale, and a short checklist for reviewers
notes: Initial audit completed 2025-09-12: identified 48 button instances with manual overrides; 12 chart/table frames with mixed spacers
Decision: prioritize touch target consistency over perfect optical alignment for tight densities (trade-off documented in Confluence)
We will keep legacy component aliases for two cycles to allow quick rollbacks for partner repos that still reference old names
Edge case: floating icon-only buttons inside dense table rows need a 6px inset to avoid overlap with row separators; handled by token alias chart-row-inset
Refer to accessibility note: target hit area >= 40px for interactive controls unless explicitly marked decorative
